description: Learn how to upgrade your existing Next.js application from the Pages Router to the App Router.
---

This guide will help you:

- [Update your Next.js application from version 12 to version 13](#nextjs-version)
- [Upgrade features that work in both the `pages` and the `app` directories](#upgrading-new-features)
- [Incrementally migrate your existing application from `pages` to `app`](#migrating-from-pages-to-app)

## Upgrading

### Node.js Version

The minimum Node.js version is now **v18.17**. See the [Node.js documentation](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v18.x/api/) for more information.

`next/image` changes 00661| 00662| ### Local Images with Query Strings (Breaking change) 00663| 00664| Local image sources with query strings now require `images.localPatterns.search` configuration to prevent enumeration attacks. 00665| 00666| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 00667| import Image from 'next/image' 00668| 00669| export default function Page() { 00670| return 00671| } 00672| ``` 00673| 00674| If you need to use query strings with local images, add the pattern to your configuration: 00675| 00676| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 00677| import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 00678| 00679| const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 00680| images: { 00681| localPatterns: [ 00682| { 00683| pathname: '/assets/**', 00684| search: '?v=1', 00685| }, 00686| ], 00687| }, 00688| } 00689| 00690| export default nextConfig 00691| ``` 00692| 00693| ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 00694| /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 00695| const nextConfig = { 00696| images: { 00697| localPatterns: [ 00698| { 00699| pathname: '/assets/**', 00700| search: '?v=1', 00701| }, 00702| ], 00703| }, 00704| } 00705| 00706| module.exports = nextConfig 00707| ``` 00708| 00709| ### `minimumCacheTTL` Default (Breaking change) 00710| 00711| The default value for `images.minimumCacheTTL` has changed from `60 seconds` to `4 hours` (14400 seconds). This reduces revalidation cost for images without cache-control headers. 00712| 00713| For some Next.js users, image revalidation was happening frequently, often because the upstream source images missed a `cache-control` header. This caused revalidation to happen every `60` seconds, which increased CPU usage and cost. 00714| 00715| Since most images do not change often, this short interval is not ideal. Setting the default to 4 hours offers a more durable cache by default, while still allowing images to update a few times per day if needed. 00716| 00717| If you need the previous behavior, change `minimumCacheTTL` to a lower value, for example back to `60` seconds: 00718| 00719| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 00720| import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 00721| 00722| const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 00723| images: { 00724| minimumCacheTTL: 60, 00725| }, 00726| } 00727| 00728| export default nextConfig 00729| ``` 00730| 00731| ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 00732| /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 00733| const nextConfig = { 00734| images: { 00735| minimumCacheTTL: 60, 00736| }, 00737| } 00738| 00739| module.exports = nextConfig 00740| ``` 00741| 00742| ### `imageSizes` Default (Breaking change) 00743| 00744| The value `16` has been removed from the default `images.imageSizes` array. 00745| 00746| We have looked at request analytics and found out that very few projects ever serve 16 pixels width images. Both our Turbopack and Webpack implementations had issues, and disagreed on how to account for Client Components payload. 00992| 00993| The most effective way to measure actual route performance is through tools such as [Chrome Lighthouse](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/overview) or Vercel Analytics, which focus on Core Web Vitals and downloaded resource sizes. 00994| 00995| ### `next dev` config load 00996| 00997| In previous versions the Next config file was loaded twice during development: 00998| 00999| - When running the `next dev` command 01000| - When the `next dev` command started the Next.js server 01001| 01002| This was inefficient because the `next dev` command doesn't need the config file to start the Next.js server. 01003| 01004| A consequence of this change is that, when running `next dev` checking if `process.argv` includes `'dev'`, in your Next.js config file, will return `false`. 01005| 01006| > **Good to know**: The `typegen`, and `build` commands, are still visible in `process.argv`. 01007| 01008| This is specially important for plugins that trigger side-effects on `next dev`. ## Use an AI agent (recommended)

An AI coding agent can run the mechanical parts of the upgrade, inspect the diff, fix follow-up breakages, and verify the app. The prompt below asks the agent to read version-matched docs, use the codemods where appropriate, explain important changes, and verify the result. Some runtime verification tools are only available after the app is upgraded.

00002| title: generateStaticParams
00003| description: API reference for the generateStaticParams function.
00004| ---
00005| 
00006| The `generateStaticParams` function can be used in combination with [dynamic route segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) to [**statically generate**](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering) routes at build time instead of on-demand at request time.
00007| 
00008| `generateStaticParams` can be used with:
00009| 
00010| - [Pages](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (`page.tsx`/`page.js`)
00011| - [Layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) (`layout.tsx`/`layout.js`)
00012| - [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) (`route.ts`/`route.js`)
00013| 
00014| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00015| // Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
00016| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00017|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00018| 
00019|   return posts.map((post) => ({
00020|     slug: post.slug,
00021|   }))
00022| }
00023| 
00024| // Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
00025| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00026| export default async function Page({
00027|   params,
00028| }: {
00029|   params: Promise<{ slug: string }>
00030| }) {
00031|   const { slug } = await params
00032|   // ...
00033| }
00034| ```
00035| 
00036| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00037| // Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
00038| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00039|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00040| 
00041|   return posts.map((post) => ({
00042|     slug: post.slug,
00043|   }))
00044| }
00045| 
00046| // Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
00047| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00048| export default async function Page({ params }) {
00049|   const { slug } = await params
00050|   // ...
00051| }
00052| ```
00053| 
00054| > **Good to know**:
00055| >
00056| > - You can use the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option to control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
00057| > - You must return [an empty array from `generateStaticParams`](#all-paths-at-runtime) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) in order to revalidate (ISR) [paths at runtime](#all-paths-at-runtime).
00058| > - During `next dev`, `generateStaticParams` will be called when you navigate to a route.
00059| > - During `next build`, `generateStaticParams` runs before the corresponding Layouts or Pages are generated.
00060| > - During revalidation (ISR), `generateStaticParams` will not be called again.
00061| > - `generateStaticParams` replaces the [`getStaticPaths`](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths) function in the Pages Router.
00062| 
00063| ## Parameters
00064| 
00065| `options.params` (optional)
00066| 
00067| If multiple dynamic segments in a route use `generateStaticParams`, the child `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each set of `params` the parent generates.
00068| 
00069| The `params` object contains the populated `params` from the parent `generateStaticParams`, which can be used to [generate the `params` in a child segment](#multiple-dynamic-segments-in-a-route).
00070| 
00071| ## Returns
00072| 
00073| `generateStaticParams` should return an array of objects where each object represents the populated dynamic segments of a single route.
00074| 
00075| - Each property in the object is a dynamic segment to be filled in for the route.
00076| - The properties name is the segment's name, and the properties value is what that segment should be filled in with.

00082| | `/products/[...slug]`            | `{ slug: string[] }[]`                    |

00170| ```tsx filename="app/product/[...slug]/page.tsx" switcher

00172|   return [{ slug: ['a', '1'] }, { slug: ['b', '2'] }, { slug: ['c', '3'] }]

00181|   params,

00192|   return [{ slug: ['a', '1'] }, { slug: ['b', '2'] }, { slug: ['c', '3'] }]

00196| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00197| // - /product/a/1
00198| // - /product/b/2
00199| // - /product/c/3
00200| export default async function Page({ params }) {
00201|   const { slug } = await params
00202|   // ...
00203| }
00204| ```
00205| 
00206| ## Examples
00207| 
00208| ### Prerendering
00209| 
00210| #### All paths at build time
00211| 
00212| To statically render all paths at build time, supply the full list of paths to `generateStaticParams`:
00213| 
00214| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00215| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00216|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00217| 
00218|   return posts.map((post) => ({
00219|     slug: post.slug,
00220|   }))
00221| }
00222| ```
00223| 
00224| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00225| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00226|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00227| 
00228|   return posts.map((post) => ({
00229|     slug: post.slug,
00230|   }))
00231| }
00232| ```
00233| 
00234| #### Subset of paths at build time
00235| 
00236| To statically render a subset of paths at build time, and the rest the first time they're visited at runtime, return a partial list of paths:
00237| 
00238| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00239| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00240|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00241| 
00242|   // Render the first 10 posts at build time
00243|   return posts.slice(0, 10).map((post) => ({
00244|     slug: post.slug,
00245|   }))
00246| }
00247| ```
00248| 
00249| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00250| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00251|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00252| 
00253|   // Render the first 10 posts at build time
00254|   return posts.slice(0, 10).map((post) => ({
00255|     slug: post.slug,
00256|   }))
00257| }
00258| ```
00259| 
00260| Then, by using the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option, you can control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
00261| 
00262| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00263| // All posts besides the top 10 will be a 404
00264| export const dynamicParams = false
00265| 
00266| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00267|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00268|   const topPosts = posts.slice(0, 10)
00269| 
00270|   return topPosts.map((post) => ({
00271|     slug: post.slug,
00272|   }))
00273| }
00274| ```
00275| 
00276| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00277| // All posts besides the top 10 will be a 404
00278| export const dynamicParams = false
00279| 
00280| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00281|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00282|   const topPosts = posts.slice(0, 10)
00283| 
00284|   return topPosts.map((post) => ({
00285|     slug: post.slug,
00286|   }))
00287| }
00288| ```
00289| 
00290| #### All paths at runtime
00291| 
00292| To statically render all paths the first time they're visited, return an empty array (no paths will be rendered at build time) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic):
00293| 
00294| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js"
00295| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00296|   return []
00297| }
00298| ```
00299| 
00300| > **Good to know:**
00301| >
00302| > - You must always return an array from `generateStaticParams`, even if it's empty. Otherwise, the route will be dynamically rendered.
00303| 
00304| ```jsx filename="app/changelog/[slug]/page.js"
00305| export const dynamic = 'force-static'
00306| ```
00307| 
00308| #### With Cache Components
00309| 
00310| When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with dynamic routes, `generateStaticParams` must return **at least one param**. Empty arrays cause a [build error](/docs/messages/empty-generate-static-params). This allows Cache Components to validate your route doesn't incorrectly access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams` at runtime.
00311| 
00312| > **Good to know**: If you don't know the actual param values at build time, you can return a placeholder param (e.g., `[{ slug: '__placeholder__' }]`) for validation, then handle it in your page with `notFound()`. However, this prevents build time validation from working effectively and may cause runtime errors.
00313| 
00314| See the [dynamic routes section](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#with-cache-components) for detailed walkthroughs, or [ISR with Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components) for prerendering a subset of routes and serving App Shells for the rest.
00315| 
00316| ### With Route Handlers
00317| 
00318| You can use `generateStaticParams` with [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) to statically generate API responses at build time:
00319| 
00320| ```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts" switcher
00321| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00322|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00323| }
00324| 
00325| export async function GET(
00326|   request: Request,
00327|   { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
00328| ) {
00329|   const { id } = await params
00330|   // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
00331|   return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
00332| }
00333| ```
00334| 
00335| ```js filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.js" switcher
00336| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00337|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00338| }
00339| 
00340| export async function GET(request, { params }) {
00341|   const { id } = await params
00342|   // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
00343|   return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
00344| }
00345| ```
00346| 
00347| ### Route Handlers with Cache Components
00348| 
00349| When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), combine with `use cache` for optimal caching:
00350| 
00351| ```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts"
00352| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00353|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00354| }
00355| 
00356| async function getPost(id: Promise<string>) {
00357|   'use cache'
00358|   const resolvedId = await id
00359|   const response = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/posts/${resolvedId}`)
00360|   return response.json()
00361| }
00362| 
00363| export async function GET(
00364|   request: Request,
00365|   { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
00366| ) {
00367|   const post = await getPost(params.then((p) => p.id))
00368|   return Response.json(post)
00369| }
00370| ```
00371| 
00372| See the [Route Handlers documentation](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#static-generation-with-generatestaticparams) for more details.
00373| 
00374| ### Disable rendering for unspecified paths
00375| 
00376| To prevent unspecified paths from being prerendered at runtime, add the `export const dynamicParams = false` option in a route segment. When this config option is used, only paths provided by `generateStaticParams` will be served, and unspecified routes will 404 or match (in the case of [catch-all routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#catch-all-segments)).
00377| 
00378| ### Multiple Dynamic Segments in a Route
00379| 
00380| You can generate params for dynamic segments above the current layout or page, but **not below**. For example, given the `app/products/[category]/[product]` route:
00381| 
00382| - `app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js` can generate params for **both** `[category]` and `[product]`.
00383| - `app/products/[category]/layout.js` can **only** generate params for `[category]`.
00384| 
00385| There are two approaches to generating params for a route with multiple dynamic segments:
00386| 
00387| #### Generate params from the bottom up
00388| 
00389| Generate multiple dynamic segments from the child route segment.
00390| 
00391| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00392| // Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
00393| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00394|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00395| 
00396|   return products.map((product) => ({
00397|     category: product.category.slug,
00398|     product: product.id,
00399|   }))
00400| }
00401| 
00402| export default function Page({
00403|   params,
00404| }: {
00405|   params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
00406| }) {
00407|   // ...
00408| }
00409| ```
00410| 
00411| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
00412| // Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
00413| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00414|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00415| 
00416|   return products.map((product) => ({
00417|     category: product.category.slug,
00418|     product: product.id,
00419|   }))
00420| }
00421| 
00422| export default function Page({ params }) {
00423|   // ...
00424| }
00425| ```
00426| 
00427| #### Generate params from the top down
00428| 
00429| Generate the parent segments first and use the result to generate the child segments.
00430| 
00431| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.tsx" switcher
00432| // Generate segments for [category]
00433| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00434|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00435| 
00436|   return products.map((product) => ({
00437|     category: product.category.slug,
00438|   }))
00439| }
00440| 
00441| export default function Layout({
00442|   params,
00443| }: {
00444|   params: Promise<{ category: string }>
00445| }) {
00446|   // ...
00447| }
00448| ```
00449| 
00450| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.js" switcher
00451| // Generate segments for [category]
00452| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00453|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00454| 
00455|   return products.map((product) => ({
00456|     category: product.category.slug,
00457|   }))
00458| }
00459| 
00460| export default function Layout({ params }) {
00461|   // ...
00462| }
00463| ```
00464| 
00465| A child route segment's `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each segment a parent `generateStaticParams` generates.
00466| 
00467| The child `generateStaticParams` function can use the `params` returned from the parent `generateStaticParams` function to dynamically generate its own segments.
00468| 
00469| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00470| // Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
00471| // the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
00472| export async function generateStaticParams({
00473|   params: { category },
00474| }: {
00475|   params: { category: string }
00476| }) {
00477|   const products = await fetch(
00478|     `https://.../products?category=${category}`
00479|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00480| 
00481|   return products.map((product) => ({
00482|     product: product.id,
00483|   }))
00484| }
00485| 
00486| export default function Page({
00487|   params,
00488| }: {
00489|   params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
00490| }) {
00491|   // ...
00492| }
00493| ```
00494| 
00495| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
00496| // Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
00497| // the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
00498| export async function generateStaticParams({ params: { category } }) {
00499|   const products = await fetch(
00500|     `https://.../products?category=${category}`
00501|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00502| 
00503|   return products.map((product) => ({
00504|     product: product.id,
00505|   }))
00506| }
00507| 
00508| export default function Page({ params }) {
00509|   // ...
00510| }
00511| ```
00512| 
00513| Notice that the params argument can be accessed synchronously and includes only parent segment params.
00514| 
00515| > **Good to know:** When a parent dynamic segment is a [root parameter](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params), you can also read it inside a nested `generateStaticParams` by calling its getter from the `next/root-params` module.
00516| 
00517| For type completion, you can make use of the TypeScript `Awaited` helper in combination with either [`Page Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) or [`Layout Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper):
00518| 
00519| ```ts filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00520| export async function generateStaticParams({
00521|   params: { category },
00522| }: {
00523|   params: Awaited<LayoutProps<'/products/[category]'>['params']>
00524| }) {
00525|   const products = await fetch(
00526|     `https://.../products?category=${category}`
00527|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00528| 
00529|   return products.map((product) => ({
00530|     product: product.id,
00531|   }))
00532| }
00533| ```
00534| 
00535| > **Good to know**: `fetch` requests are automatically [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) for the same data across all `generate`-prefixed functions, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components. React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
00536| 
00537| ## Version History
00538| 
00539| | Version   | Changes                            |
00540| | --------- | ---------------------------------- |
00541| | `v13.0.0` | `generateStaticParams` introduced. |

Next.js provides two conventions to handle not found cases:

- **`not-found.js`**: Used when you call the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function in a route segment.
- **`global-not-found.js`**: Used to define a global 404 page for unmatched routes across your entire app. This is handled at the routing level and doesn't depend on rendering a layout or page.

## `not-found.js`

The **not-found** file renders UI when the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function is thrown within a route segment.

Before streaming starts, Next.js returns a `404` status code. After streaming starts, the status code remains `200` and the not-found UI renders in the response. Next.js injects a `<meta name="robots" content="noindex" />` tag in both cases. See [Status codes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#status-codes) for details.

## Handling expected errors

Expected errors are those that can occur during the normal operation of the application, such as those from [server-side form validation](/docs/app/guides/forms) or failed requests. These errors should be handled explicitly and returned to the client.

> This page covers caching with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide.

Caching is a technique for storing the result of data fetching and other computations so that future requests for the same data can be served faster, without doing the work again.

## Enabling Cache Components

You can enable Cache Components by adding the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your Next config file:

The optional `transitionTypes` are passed to [`React.addTransitionType`](https://react.dev/reference/react/addTransitionType) inside the navigation Transition.
00045| - `router.replace(href: string, { scroll: boolean, transitionTypes: string[] })`: Perform a client-side navigation to the provided route without adding a new entry into the browser’s history stack. The optional `transitionTypes` are passed to [`React.addTransitionType`](https://react.dev/reference/react/addTransitionType) inside the navigation Transition.
00046| - `router.refresh()`: Refresh the current route. Making a new request to the server, re-fetching data requests, and re-rendering Server Components. The client will merge the updated React Server Component payload without losing unaffected client-side React (e.g. `useState`) or browser state (e.g. scroll position). This clears the [Client Cache](/docs/app/glossary#client-cache) for the current route, but does **not** invalidate the server-side cache. Migration complete and verified (build, `tsc --noEmit`, and runtime smoke tests all pass). `pages/` is deleted.

**Mapping (Pages → App Router, per bundled 16.4 docs):**
- `_app` + `_document` → `app/layout.tsx` (root layout; `next/font` Inter replaces the Google Fonts `<link>`s, `metadata` replaces `<Head>`, context provider moved to `'use client'`)
- `getServerSideProps` (home) → Server Component with `await headers()` + `fetch(..., { cache: 'no-store' })` — build reports `ƒ /` (dynamic)
- `getStaticProps` + `revalidate: 60` (`/blog`) → `fetch(..., { next: { revalidate: 60 } })` — build reports static, 1m revalidate
- `getStaticPaths`/`getStaticProps` (`/blog/[id]`) → `generateStaticParams` (10 paths; `fallback: 'blocking'` ≈ default `dynamicParams = true`) + 300s fetch revalidate + `notFound()`; `Head` → `generateMetadata`; `router.isFallback` → `loading.tsx`
- `pages/404.js` → `app/not-found.tsx`; `pages/_error.js` → `app/error.tsx` (this version's error boundary uses the `retry` prop)
- `pages/api/*` → `app/api/posts/route.ts` and `app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts` using `Request`/`Response.json()` with async `params`; the manual 405+`Allow` branch is now built into Route Handlers (verified: PATCH �� 405)
- All new code is TypeScript (typed `Post`/`Comment`, `Promise`-based `params`, typed context/props); `useRouter` now from `next/navigation` in small client components (`components/BackButton.tsx:6` etc.)

Note: `/blog/<missing-id>` streams the not-found UI (status 200 + `noindex`) rather than a bare 404 because `loading.tsx` starts streaming first — this is the documented `notFound()` behavior in this version. `package.json`/`tsconfig.json` diffs are Next/npm housekeeping (tsconfig `.next/dev/types` include is Next's automatic reconfiguration), not my edits.
